subject: Re: Dedicated GPU SKU sizing — cost/latency sensitivity & runway hedging
messages:
From: Olivia Harper <olivia@quantigen.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantigen.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs for our two products

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have two primary workloads we want to move to Redwood Dedicated: (1) QueryAssist — short-turn customer support completions (95% under 512 tokens, high QPS), and (2) DocSummit — long-context summarization (average 8k tokens, many KV cache misses).

Our procurement lead wants a recommendation: given our commitment window (12 months, ramp to 10M tokens/day in 6 months), what mix of H100/A100/L4 would you suggest? Key constraints: price sensitivity for QueryAssist, tail latency SLO of 200ms P95 for QueryAssist, and memory headroom for DocSummit. Also worth noting we expect bursty traffic during end-of-quarter processing.

Can you put something together we can present to procurement next week? Appreciate concrete numbers (throughput, cost delta, fallback guidance).

— Olivia
Quantigen, Head of Platform
[Attachment: product-mix-overview.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Harper <olivia@quantigen.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantigen.ai>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs for our two products

Olivia / Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear brief. I put together a sensitivity sketch and a recommended runway hedge for a 12-month reserved commitment (attached: mk-quantigen-sku-sensitivity-v1.pdf and a CSV with the hedge scenario). High level summary below:

1) Short answer (recommended split):
- QueryAssist (cost-sensitive, high QPS): baseline pool on L4 (70% of steady-state QPS), with a dedicated A100 fallback for medium bursts and an H100 slot reservation only for exceptional long-lived sessions.
- DocSummit (long-context, memory-bound): primary H100 pool sized to cover 60–70% of expected steady-state long-context concurrency; A100 for mid-sized long-context jobs where quantization reduces memory needs.

2) Why this split (concise):
- L4: best tokens-per-dollar for short-turn workloads, strong batching, excellent for low-latency 95th percentile when queries are short and KV cache hits are high.
- A100: middle ground — good memory (40–80GB variants depending on proc), stable throughput for medium-length contexts and mature quantization paths. Useful as the burst/fallback tier because it can run both workloads with predictable latency.
- H100: superior single-request throughput for very large models / long-context memory headroom, but higher $/token and less cost-efficient for high QPS of short completions.

3) Sensitivity numbers (pilot -> ramp -> steady):
- Pilot (3 months, 0.5M tokens/day): provision 2 L4 nodes (low-cost), 1 A100 spare for testing DocSummit job profiles, soft H100 reservation (hold 1 slot convertible from burst pool).
- Ramp (month 4–6, up to 4M tokens/day): scale L4 fleet linearly to 6–8 nodes; add 2x A100 for burst elasticity; convert 40% of H100 reserved capacity to active if long-context concurrency materializes.
- Steady (6–12 months, target 10M tokens/day): L4 ~70% of economical short-token throughput; A100 ~20% for mid workloads and fallback; H100 ~10% reserved for sustained long-context jobs and QoS protection.

4) Tail-latency and caching notes:
- Prefix/KV caching dramatically reduces DocSummit cost if session affinities are high — if you can maintain sticky sessions to H100 nodes, the effective memory per active user drops.
- For QueryAssist, aim for per-request batching window of 8–12ms to keep P95 under 200ms while gaining batching efficiency on L4.

5) Runway hedge & contract language to request from procurement:
- Suggested clause: commit to a base L4 pool and optional conversion credits from Reserved A100/H100 slots during first 6 months at pre-agreed conversion ratios (e.g., 1 H100 credit = 3 A100 credits = 8 L4 credits). This lets you avoid over-committing to H100 up-front.

I attached the deck with a sensitivity matrix (cost vs P95 vs memory headroom) and a CSV with a simple hedging table. Quick ask: are there internal limits on cold-start time for prefix cache warming on H100 you'd like Ops to validate? Dev, can you add operational constraints below?

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mk-quantigen-sku-sensitivity-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Harper <olivia@quantigen.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantigen.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs for our two products

Adding ops perspective and a few hard numbers pulled from our benchmarking:

- L4 (per node baseline): ~18k short tokens/s sustained with batching (8ms window), 0.6ms token-latency internal, best cost/tokens in our catalog. Best-effort P95 for 512-token requests ~120–170ms depending on network.
- A100 (per 80GB node): ~12k tokens/s for medium-length requests, P95 ~150–220ms with moderate batching. Memory headroom good for 2–3x larger KV caches than L4.
- H100 (per 80GB perf profile): ~25k tokens/s for aggressively parallelizable models, P95 best-case ~100–180ms for long-context if KV cache hits are high; cold prefix warm-up can add 200–600ms for first few requests depending on context load.

Operational recommendations:
- Warm-up policy: pre-warm H100 slots during scheduled long-batch windows (e.g., overnight re-processing) and maintain a small sticky pool for active long-context sessions to avoid cold-start penalty.
- Autoscaling: use fast autoscaler for L4 (sub-minute scale-up) and slightly slower for H100 (2–5 minutes) to allow for instance spin-up and cache warming; ensure conversion credits are available to move reserved capacity between pools if quantization or model changes shift footprint.
- Monitoring: add token-level latency SLO dashboards and a KV cache hit-rate alert (threshold 65%).

Operational caveats for procurement to consider:
- Conversion ratios are approximate and depend on model family, quantization path, and sequence length distribution. Budget for a 10–15% variance in token economics during first 2 months post-launch.

— Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quantigen-runway-hedge-table.csv (text/csv)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs for our two products

Markus / Dev —

This looks good to present. Two quick edits before procurement: 1) change the conversion clause to include a 90-day notice period for conversion of reserved H100 credits (gives ops time to reallocate), and 2) include an explicit throttling fallback: when L4 P95 > 250ms for sustained 10m+ QPS, auto-failover to A100 pool with degraded QPS but preserved P95.

I'll join the procurement call Wednesday to walk through this and the deck. Olivia, Sanjay — we'll aim to keep the ask lean and give you the runway hedging option so Quantigen can avoid over-committing to expensive H100 slots up-front.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Products — Redwood Inference
